chapter: Basie and life on the road
title: Rehearsals, reading and the most demanding bands
summary: Basie readers best; Hampton rehearsed daily because of stage fright; Ray hard on his men.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: This is reel number six with Wallace Davenport, November 11, 1995. So what I'm saying is that you, moving from band to band, I think it said you had to have, your reading had to be really, really, really good. Oh yeah. That's right.

Good. Because when we recorded with Ray, we had to rehearse. Now Ray's band were good readers, but they weren't the kind of readers Basie's band was. And Basie had better readers than Duke. Because we played for Frank Sinatra and we played for Tony Bennett. Both of them said, they don't have any trouble, they don't have any problems with basic bands reading the music. They don't have too many problems with Duke. But sometimes they had to go over the number
twice or three times. Now which bands used to rehearse a lot? What bands?

Lionel Hampton. He rehearse, every day that you work, whether you need it or not. And the purpose was? I found out the real purpose why he rehearsed so much. See one time when I got back with the band I said, look, I'm going to make one rehearsal a week. And if I make more than one rehearsal a week, I want to get paid for the rehearsal. So one day he didn't rehearse, and he had to play Midnight Sun, this is the thing that he wrote. And he played that every night. He couldn't play it. See like when he, because he gets nervous, stage fright. As long as he's been playing he gets stage fright. But see if he go out there and rehearse, and then go and change, and the fellas go eat and change clothes and come back, it's just like coming back off intermission. You're not starting off new. But for him to get on that stage and just play without rehearsing, he gets nervous, and messes up. As good as he is? Mm-hmm. Dinah Washington was just about the same way. She had to curse the audience out. She cursed the audience for talking. But after that she's relaxed, you know. Ella Fitzgerald, she was nervous too. She was stage fright. Right. So which of all the bands, which was the most

demanding, was it, that you played with in road bands? Demanding in which way? In music, musically demanding. Who was the most musically demanding? Basie. Basie. And was he hard on you as a disciplinarian, as a person?

Mm-mm. He wasn't hard on anybody. He was one of the nicest band leaders, I mean, as far as getting along with the guy. But not a waste guy, it was Ray Charles. Some of those guys, he would talk to them like a dog. But they left themselves open for it. Some of the guys would spin up all their money, and all have money to check out the hotels, and that'd make a bad name for a band. And so, Ray, Ray didn't like the idea of those guys not paying the rent. A lot of them didn't pay the rent.
